blockers.claim: authorizationRecord.doctorV4FieldMapping is total and preserves the exact authorization/admission basis in the mandatory post-report.
blockers.evidence: The frozen schema declares 19 closed authorization members. Mechanical comparison against doctorV4FieldMapping finds two absent keys: actor and actionSubtype. The mapping entries for productAdmissionRefs, designContractRef, and owners explicitly say they are not consentRecords members; unlike consentCarrier, they name no residualLimitation or other destination. doctor v4's record has only id, actionClass, permissionRef, scope, endpoint, bytes, authorization, execution, result, residualLimitation, effectOutcome, enforcementDisclosure, and argumentVector. The authorization record is expressly not journaled and does not survive the invocation. Therefore a report cannot round-trip the exact subtype, recorded contract digest, product-admission digest/selector/standing, or responsible owners. This contradicts doctorV4FieldMapping.rule's own statement that an unmapped member is a defect, and it defeats the auditability promised by FC-STALE-CONTRACT-REF. The same mapping also cannot prove that a CA-3/CA-4 report retained the subtype against which product admission was evaluated.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a real 19/19 serialization. Map actor and actionSubtype into closed doctor-v4 fields or a closed nested scope shape; preserve designContractRef, productAdmissionRefs, and owners in the post-report or in a separately durable authorization record linked by an exact id. Reconcile denied/no-consent authorization records with doctor v4's consentRecords cardinality. Add round-trip fixtures that fail when subtype, contract digest, admission digest, standing, or owner evidence is dropped or relabeled. Do not call the mapping total while a member is absent or intentionally discarded.

blockers.claim: The CA-2 customer-tool branch is fail-closed for tool-originated egress after being removed from PT-NET-EGRESS.
blockers.evidence: ES-2b correctly says a customer tool is not a component, cannot use PT-NET-EGRESS, and cannot borrow host CA-4. PATH-SPAWNED-TOOL-EGRESS and FC-HOST-CA4-NOT-TOOL-SOCKET, however, refuse only a 'network-capable' CA-2 execution. No authorization member, product-admission shape, FC-C1..C6 gate, or fixture defines or verifies network capability or requires enforced no-network confinement. Accepted doctor v4 CA-2 says the customer tool is outside the signed closure and doctor cannot state what it reads, writes, or sends. Its consentDoesNotCascade.theHardCase permits a declared-local-only CA-2 target under CA-2 alone while expressly disclosing that no-egress is declared and not enforced; for a declared-networked target it says a separate CA-4 is the prerequisite. v3 simultaneously says that CA-4 can never authorize the tool's socket. Thus a DR-119-approved tool can pass the six v3 gates under a local-only declaration and still send a packet for which v3 names no authority. The new actor label is correct, but the execution rule is not closed.
blockers.requiredRepair: For the architecture preview, either make every CA-2 customer-tool execution unexercisable because its network behavior is unbounded, or require demonstrated no-network confinement as a closed product-admission condition before CA-2 can pass. A future tool-egress lane must be a distinct D-000 product/authorization decision and may not borrow host CA-4 or PT-NET-EGRESS. Explicitly reconcile or supersede doctor v4's separate-CA-4/local-only recital. Add a negative fixture in which a tool declared local-only opens a socket.

blockers.claim: The host-effect contract covers the full accepted doctor-v4 CA-1 host actor surface.
blockers.evidence: doctor v4 defines CA-1 as either spawning an admitted component executable or running component code in-process, and its actor analysis places the whole in-process variant on the host side. v3's coveredActs.CA-1-host-head covers only the decision to spawn, its componentGenerationIdentity semantics bind bytes 'actually spawned', actionSubtype must be null for CA-1, effectCommit supplies only an OS child-process creation boundary, and actorSet excludes only admitted child processes. No v3 byte classifies, denies, commits, or reports the in-process variant. Relabeling it CA-1-HOST-HEAD would apply a nonexistent OS-acceptance boundary and a false child-tail statement; leaving it outside that value makes an accepted doctor-v4 departure unrepresentable without an explicit denial.
blockers.requiredRepair: Either state normatively that CA-1 in-process execution is unexercisable in the architecture preview and add a fail-closed fixture, or add a closed CA-1 execution-form/subtype with exact generation/manifest binding, an honest in-process commit boundary, outcome rules, product admission, and doctor-v4 mapping. Reconcile coveredActs and effectCommit with the accepted doctor-v4 CA-1 definition.

blockers.claim: The CA-4 commit boundary prevents DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED after any irreversible doctor-network effect.
blockers.evidence: v3 defines CA-4 commit as 'The first byte has been handed to the kernel or network stack' and globally maps cancellation before commit to DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED. Accepted doctor v4's no-network property covers opening a socket and resolving a name as well as sending bytes, with CA-4 as the only departure. DNS lookup and connection establishment can emit DNS packets, TCP SYNs, QUIC packets, or TLS metadata before doctor hands an application payload byte to the kernel. A receive path also has no host-to-kernel first-byte handoff. Cancellation or death after one of those effects but before the stated boundary can therefore be reported DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED even though the host has disclosed itself or contacted an endpoint. endpointSet also does not state how resolver endpoints are included in exact scope.
blockers.requiredRepair: Move CA-4 commit to OS acceptance of the first operation capable of causing network observation, including name resolution, connect/handshake, send, and receive, and map unknown acceptance to INDETERMINATE. Define exact endpoint scope for resolution and connection intermediaries. Add cancel/death fixtures after DNS or connect acceptance but before application payload, plus receive-before-observation.

advisories.claim: OPEN-NOT-ADMITTED and UNOWNED are used consistently once an accountable admission owner is named.

advisories.suggestedRepair: Use OPEN-NOT-ADMITTED wherever the accountable authority is already named; reserve UNOWNED for a surface that actually needs D-000 owner assignment. Make BLK-2 and the named CA-4 path recitals match the subtype records.
